The reductions affect an area where more than two-thirds of the population faces acute hunger.

The White House described the waivers as serving U.S. national interests, while leaving earlier Russia-related sanctions intact. The move prompted criticism from Ukrainian and EU leaders, who argue that pressure on Russian energy revenue should be maintained as Ukraine seeks support for winter energy, air-defense and financing needs.

stories.title: Trump Suspends New Russia Sanctions Amid Tensions with Zelensky
stories.summary: The US president has temporarily waived several recently enacted sanctions against Russia, citing national interest. This decision has drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, who expressed concern that it would embolden Russia's military actions. Trump did not provide further details on the rationale behind the suspension.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump waived several new U.S. sanctions and duties targeting Russia, invoking the national interest while leaving earlier Russia-related executive-order sanctions in place. The move pauses measures aimed at Russian goods, officials, banks, energy activity and sanctions evasion. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the decision, saying it could encourage Russia to continue killing and would not help end the war; that is his assessment rather than a demonstrated outcome.

stories.title: Violence Erupts as Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians During Olive Harvest in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers launched coordinated attacks on Palestinian villages in the West Bank during the annual olive harvest, resulting in injuries to several Palestinians and a Washington Post journalist. The settlers reportedly set fire to cars and olive trees, while also throwing rocks and using clubs against those attempting to harvest olives. The violence has been described as part of a pattern of yearly disruptions during the harvest season.
stories.event_title: US Ambassador Visits Palestinian Town Affected by Settler Violence

story_report.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian farmers during the West Bank olive harvest, with reports that cars and olive trees were burned and multiple people injured. A Washington Post journalist was among those attacked. Video and witness accounts cited by the newspaper described masked men arriving from the direction of a hilltop settlement, setting groves alight and assaulting villagers and journalists. Israeli police said they were deploying investigators with IDF forces to gather evidence and testimony.

stories.title: Three Men Sentenced to 158 Years for Murdering Surfers in Mexico
stories.summary: A Mexican judge has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the murders of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad. The trio was killed during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024, reportedly during an attempted robbery.
stories.event_title: Three Men Convicted for Murdering Australian Brothers and US Friend in Mexico

story_report.summary: A Mexican court sentenced Jesús Gerardo García, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the killings of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend, Carter Rhoad. The men were convicted of murder, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence over the deaths during the group’s 2024 surfing trip in Baja California. The sentencing followed guilty verdicts delivered a week earlier, with the court finding the defendants acted with premeditation.

stories.title: Fast-Moving Fires Destroy Coastal Homes in Southern California
stories.summary: A fast-moving fire in Southern California, fueled by high winds, has destroyed at least six homes along the coast. The flames prompted thousands of residents to evacuate as the fire spread rapidly, affecting expensive properties in the area.
stories.event_title: California Wildfire

story_report.summary: A fast-moving, wind-fueled fire near San Clemente destroyed at least six coastal homes and forced thousands of people to evacuate. California officials said the fire began shortly after 11:30 a.m. on Oct. 16 and had burned about 465 acres by that evening. The latest CAL FIRE update from that day put containment at 0%, while evacuation orders covered parts of San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano.

stories.title: Children Bear Heavy Toll in DRC's Severe Ebola Outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing its deadliest Ebola outbreak, with children particularly affected. Reports indicate that more than 1 in 4 of the deaths are among children, who face a staggering 60% fatality rate. This outbreak is caused by a rare strain of the virus for which there is currently no approved treatment.

The Aden airport was struck by two missiles late on Friday, marking the second such incident in less than two weeks.
